title: Function calling parse debug scratchpad - incident breadcrumbs
content:
TL;DR: intermittent failures where model responses intended as function call arguments contain extra text or truncated JSON, causing downstream parse errors. Repro steps, logs, commands tried, hypotheses and quick workarounds below. Mostly a scratchpad - messy, but useful breadcrumbs for post-mortem and follow-ups.

Incident context:
- First noticed 2026-01-12 during a canary rollout of small LLM variant for reranking pipeline.
- Symptoms: 2-5% of requests with function call enabled return an assistant message that claims to call the function but the arguments payload is invalid JSON or has stray characters ("--" or explanatory text) before/after JSON.
- Downstream effect: parser raises a JSON parse exception; route falls back to text-only handling which increases latency and degrades quality.

Repro steps (deterministic-ish):
1) Use model: small-v2-debug (can reproduce on hosted test env and locally with containerized runtime).
2) Prompt: system + user with function definitions (single function: generate_rerank) + user messages containing list of items to rank.
3) Call the API with function_call="auto" and streaming disabled.
4) Observe response: assistant.role = "assistant", content empty, function_call.name = "generate_rerank", function_call.arguments string sometimes malformed.

Example error snippets (copied raw):
- "function_call.arguments": "{\n  \"items\": [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"],\n  \"context\": \"user query\"\n} -- note: confidence low"
- "ParseError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" (happened when the arguments string started with "\n\nNote:" or when there was a stray BOM)
- "Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0" (one case where HTML snippet was inserted by model commentary)

Commands / experiments tried (chronological):
- 2026-01-13 10:20: prompt -> added a strict instruction: "ONLY output the JSON string matching the function schema, no commentary." Result: error rate dropped from ~3.4% -> ~2.1% (improvement but not eliminated).
- 2026-01-13 14:05: wrapped the function signature with additional examples of valid output. Result: minor improvement, some cases still include trailing commentary.
- 2026-01-14 09:30: forced function_call.name = explicit (instead of auto) to see if model decided to textually explain. No meaningful change.
- 2026-01-14 11:00: added content-length filter to downstream parser to detect obviously too-long strings before JSON parse (quick guard). Catches ~15% of bad payloads but many are only slight deviations.
- 2026-01-15 16:40: switched to streaming=true to see partial tokens. Observed commentary appended AFTER JSON in stream fragments (i.e., model sent JSON then appended explanation as separate tokens). This suggests generation includes both but the assistant role still marks the entire block as function_call.arguments.
- 2026-01-16 08:30: tested with temperature=0.0 and top_p=0.0. Error reduced but not zero - some hallucinated notes persisted.
- 2026-01-18: tried schema-validated function signature (explicit JSON schema in function description). Some improvement; still occasional extra text like "(see above)" appended.

Logs / raw traces (selected):
- Request id: req-20260114-0342
  model: small-v2-debug
  function defs: generate_rerank(items: list[str], context: str)
  assistant message.function_call.arguments (raw): "{\"items\":[\"x\",\"y\"].,\"context\":\"q\"} Note: confidence 0.8"
- Request id: req-20260115-1921
  assistant streaming chunk sequence: {"delta": "{\"items\": [\"a\", "}, {"delta": " \"b\", \"c\"]}"}, {"delta":"\n\nNote: the model is unsure"} -> parser concatenated chunks and got trailing text.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Model sometimes emits explanatory tokens after the JSON blob (intentional commentary) and runtime bundles them into function_call.arguments because function_call is the last output channel.
- H2: Some variants of tokenizer produce non-printing characters (BOM, ZERO-WIDTH-SPACE) that break strict JSON parsers.
- H3: Prompt/instruction enforcement is not strict enough for some rare temperature/stochastic outputs; decoding/beam behavior allows short commentary tokens.
- H4: There may be an edge case in streaming assembly code that doesn't separate function_call chunk from assistant commentary chunk when both are produced in same reply.

Quick workarounds applied in prod (temporary):
- 1) Pre-parse sanitizer: attempt to locate first balanced JSON object in the arguments string using a cheap bracket-matching heuristic (find first '{' and match until bracket count returns to zero). If found, pass that substring to json.loads. This handles many trailing-comment cases.
- 2) Fallback to regex extraction for schema-like patterns (e.g., "items": \[). Risky but reduces error rate.
- 3) Conservative dedupe: if function_call present but json.loads fails, reroute to a non-blocking re-call with temperature=0 and instruct model to output only JSON; this is slow but keeps correctness.

Root-cause investigations to pursue:
- Verify how assistant function_call.tokens are produced in streaming: confirm whether the model can switch channels mid-response (i.e., produce function_call content then produce assistant text in same response) and how runtime maps tokens to function_call.arguments.
- Inspect tokenizer output for any control characters or BOM in failing examples. Add a binary/hex dump of the argument string for a few failing requests.
- Cross-check model checkpoints/variants to identify whether this is more common on smaller quantized variants (small-v2-debug) vs baseline. Early signals show it's more frequent on quantized small models.
- Confirm whether the function schema passed to the model contains both schema and human-facing description; try trimming description to minimal.

Proposed long-term fixes:
- Server-side: add stricter validation at runtime that treats function_call.arguments as the JSON payload only up to the first balanced JSON object; log the tail for analysis and alert if tail length > threshold.
- SDK: provide an option for auto-sanitization that attempts bracket-matching extraction, with a clearly documented safety caveat.
- Model-side: work with applied-ml to update instruction tuning so that when function_call is triggered, any tokens after the JSON object are suppressed / discouraged (or mapped to a separate assistant message channel).
- Monitoring: emit metric "function_call_parse_fail_rate" and tag by model, version, region; set pager threshold at 0.5% for customer-facing routes.

Next steps / actionable TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Ashwin: add binary dump pipeline for 50 failing examples and attach to INF-321 (due 2026-02-01).
- [ ] Ethan: instrument streaming assembler to print token channel boundaries in dev logs (due 2026-02-03).
- [ ] Me (Maya): implement bracket-extract sanitizer in SDK as opt-in and run A/B test on staging (due 2026-02-10).
- [ ] Eng-APPLIED-ML: schedule sync to discuss instruction-tuning tweaks for function calls (tentative 2026-02-12).

Notes / random findings:
- Found one failure where the arguments string started with "\ufeff" (BOM). json.loads failed in Python but stripping BOM fixed it. Add small sanitizer to strip common invisible characters.
- A few cases include HTML snips; likely model hallucinated references. Those are harder to rescue via heuristics.
- For streaming, chunk boundaries sometimes split inside Unicode multibyte char -> assembly produced broken UTF-8 which then failed parse. Need to ensure we concatenate streams at byte-level carefully.

Incident breadcrumbs (for post-mortem):
- 2026-01-12: initial alert - spike in rerank errors on canary.
- 2026-01-13: attempted prompt lock-down, minor improvement.
- 2026-01-15: enabled streaming capture for detailed traces.
- 2026-01-18: applied sanitizer + fallback re-call in prod for canary routes.
- 2026-02-01: escalate to applied-ml after aggregator shows persistent ~0.8% failure on quantized small variants.

If nothing else, keep these raw examples - they are useful for model debugging and for a clear reproduction set. Will convert the best 20 failing examples into a dataset for instruction tuning.

Scratch / commands I ran locally (for reproducing quickly):
- curl -X POST https://api.internal.test/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"small-v2-debug","messages": [...],"functions": [...],"function_call":"auto","temperature":0.0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
- python local_stream_assemble.py --log-tokens --req req-20260115-1921 > trace-req-20260115-1921.log

Misc: keep this file as living scratchpad. Will move cleaned summary to confluence INF-FunctionCalling-Postmortem once root cause is nailed.

End of scratchpad.
